matchups.recap:
Rome-ans 10:9-10 ran this one like a backfield clinic, with Braelon Allen going like a woodsman running to the camp store on the way to 22.3 and Jaylen Warren and Josh Jacobs chipping in 20-plus apiece. All that came with Lamar Jackson posting a flat 0.0, a number that should sink a cabin, and the Lone Eagle still had all the arrows in the bullseye anyway. Call it a well-earned Tuna Casserole, and a reminder that depth wins camp activities even when your quarterback decides to sit out the hike entirely.

Team Bradford got a Boss outing from Jordan Love and Harold Fannin Jr., but Bijan Robinson turned in 7.6 points on an 18.16 projection and the whole operation never recovered. That cabin is stuck on the Point and Back for another week running, a losing streak now fully official, and Campcraft Enthusiast's game plan looked Stuck in the Sewards from the opening whistle. Two games lost in a row is no longer bad luck, it's a pattern, and the counselor better find some new trail markers before next week's activity.

Paralegal ran cabin activities with a steady hand this week, and Counsel's backfield rotation did the heavy lifting on the hike. D'Andre Swift went like a woodsman running to the camp store on his way to 26.9, Jahmyr Gibbs added 23.8, and Chuba Hubbard chipped in 21.4 — three Woodsman Chiefs carrying the load while the rest of 55 Burgers coasted to a well-earned Tuna Casserole. That's three Guide Recs in one lineup, and it shows what happens when a counselor actually has a feel for the week instead of just hoping for one.

Ricky Huns got a Boss outing from Tee Higgins (32.5) and a respectable showing from Michael Wilson, but everything after that was Bushwhacking without a compass. Caleb Williams under center managed just 13.98, and the supporting cast around him looked like a Woodsman playing Chief Tyler Hallenbeck in Tetherball all afternoon. Other Nate's game plan never adjusted, the deficit only widened, and this cabin heads back to the bunks having gone on a losing Bust Hike of their own making.

This week's orienteering exercise matched 46er against Old balls, and it was Boss Section Chief who came prepared with a map, a compass, and apparently a direct line to Joe Burrow, who torched the course for 39.48 points. Bhayshul Tuten added 28.9 and the Jaguars D/ST chipped in 21.0, and the Island Gudge carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike all the way to a 143.18 outing. Tyler Warren was the lone soft spot, Dutch Ovening his way to 3.8 against a projection of 8.74, but nobody at this campsite was losing sleep over it.

Old balls, meanwhile, got a respectable showing from Drake Maye, Bucky Irving, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but Kyle Pitts Sr. Walked on the alpine vegetation at 1.6 points and dragged the whole operation down with him. Funk that Junk's 110.36 would have won plenty of weeks at camp — just not this one, against a Section Chief running on all cylinders. Boss Section Chief earned his sticky buns on Sunday morning; Old balls heads home to dry out the tent.

This week's swimming instruction award goes to Blue Ridge, who put together 130.98 points behind Kirk Cousins at 28.18, Tony Pollard at 27.2, and Ja'Marr Chase at 25.6, earning a post hike scrub and then some. Even a Dutch Oven afternoon from Zay Flowers couldn't slow things down. Forty and a half points is the largest margin anyone posted across camp this week, so by lodge decree: Blue Ridge, I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

Flame On, meanwhile, never found a feel for the week. James Cook III and Dalton Kincaid turned in Boss afternoons, but Parker Washington's 3.1 against a 13.88 projection left the cabin gonna need to patch those leaves with more holes — this team got soaking wet, and the whole operation chose the Canoe Hike from kickoff on. Ninety points sounds respectable until you remember who was standing across the lake. Better scouting next week, counselor.

This week's woodcraft contest pitted Catalina Wine Mixon against Chef Boyardee, and Stefanowitzc's cabin ran a post hike scrub from the opening whistle. Tyler Allgeier carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 33.6, Brock Bowers chipped in 24.7, and Dak Prescott added 19.8, more than enough cushion to survive Jonathan Taylor's trail cheese and salami afternoon and a Chris Godwin Jr. Dutch Oven that would've sunk a lesser plan.

Catalina Wine Mixon, meanwhile, got a Guide Rec from Mahomes and McBride but everything behind them walked on the alpine vegetation — Charbonnet, Love, and Dobbins combined for barely nine points on double-digit projections, the kind of soaking wet backfield performance that no quarterback can paddle through alone. Sixty-nine and change won't cut it most weeks, and with Jordan Addison rotting on the bench this one was Bushwhacking without a compass all afternoon. Chief Ron Voice: "I'm disappointed in you."

home.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
The Machine Knows ran things like a Boss G12 Member defending a Preseason Power Ranking, letting Josh Allen carry the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 26.56 while Puka Nacua and Matthew Golden rounded out a lineup with all the arrows in the bullseye. Javonte Williams and Tre Tucker both no-showed the trip entirely, but it hardly mattered against a camp this overmatched — an easy post hike scrub of a win built on preparation, not fortune.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare is stuck on the Point and Back, dragging a losing streak further into the Sewards with another lineup that got its lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow. Drake London's 1.3 and Tez Johnson's donut turned this into a gonna-need-more-leaves situation fast, and Corey Kiner never got out of the canoe. Sixty-seven and change is Chief Ron Voice territory — I'm disappointed in you, counselor, go find a compass before next week.

headline: Week 8 results are in, underdogs had a day
